report.summary: The change makes pagination skip an item. The offset the handlers take (validateOffset, then `.offset(start)` in apps/tempo/src/artifacts/issues.ts) is a SQL OFFSET: the number of rows to skip. That means `offset + bounded.length` already points at the first item that was not returned. Adding `+ 1` silently drops one issue or comment at every page boundary. It also breaks the existing test in agent-issues.cases.ts, which expects `nextOffset` to be 2 and would now get 3. No test was added and the spec was not changed. The original code was already correct.

findings.text: Off-by-one. `offset` is a skip count passed straight to the SQL OFFSET in listRepositoryIssues and listRepositoryIssueComments (artifacts/issues.ts:160-182 and :279-288). After returning `bounded.length` items from position `offset`, the next unreturned item is at `offset + bounded.length`. With `+ 1`, each follow-up page skips one item: the first item that was cut by the byte limit, or item 51 of a full 50-item page. The agent never sees that issue or comment. Revert to `offset + bounded.length`.

The existing test `bounds large comment pages with a usable next offset` expects `first.nextOffset` to be 2. With this change it gets 3, and the second page loses an item. That breaks `bun run test` (CLAUDE.md rule 15). If a skip really was intended, CLAUDE.md rule 16 also requires a spec change and an updated test; neither is in the diff.
